service_boundary: Represents Requesty's routing service, not the upstream providers it forwards to or the models they publish.
regional_controls: A European endpoint is documented on every plan, so requests can be kept within an EU routing path.
retention_controls: The privacy policy states that customer data is not used to train models and describes this as absolute on paid plans; logs are encrypted and held for up to thirty days, and a zero-retention mode disables logging. Models whose providers permit training are labelled and offered without charge.
routing: Routing policies cover fallback and load balancing across providers, with spend controls and guardrails including personal-data detection.
customization: The service routes existing hosted models; no customer fine-tuning or private model hosting is documented.
strengths: A European routing endpoint is offered on every plan rather than reserved for enterprise agreements.
Models whose providers permit training on inputs are labelled as such and offered at no cost, making that tradeoff explicit.
tradeoffs: The terms of service render only in a browser, so the governing text could not be read from the published page.
Documented model and provider counts differ between the vendor's own pages.
Requests cross an additional service boundary before reaching an upstream provider.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the upstream model appears on the security page, in the API documentation, or in the auto-caching guide.
response_integrity.scope: Requesty security page, for the Requesty API

upstream_disclosure.note: The sub-processor list, last updated 30 August 2026, states: "Part A lists Infrastructure Sub-processors, which we engage for every customer. Part B lists Model Providers, each of which is engaged only where, and to the extent that, you route a request to a model it operates." Part B names the model providers, from OpenAI Inc. and Anthropic PBC through DeepInfra Inc. and Alibaba Cloud.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Requesty sub-processor list, for the Requesty API

credential_handling.note: The security page states: "Credentials and API keys are stored encrypted and never logged." It does not say whether that covers customer-supplied provider keys as distinct from Requesty's own keys, which it separately describes as hashed at rest and shown in full only once.
credential_handling.scope: Requesty security page, read for bring-your-own-key provider credentials

cache_isolation.note: The auto-caching guide describes Requesty's own response cache and the security page says organisation-wide zero data retention disables it; nothing states whether prompt caches at upstream providers are scoped per customer or pooled behind Requesty's shared credentials.
cache_isolation.scope: Requesty auto-caching guide, for the Requesty API

vulnerability_disclosure.note: No security contact or disclosure policy appears on the security page, and neither requesty.ai nor docs.requesty.ai serves a security.txt file.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Requesty security page, for the Requesty API

independent_audit.note: The security page states: "Our SOC 2 Type II programme is in progress. Current certification and audit status is published at trust.requesty.ai, and we make no representation of certification beyond what is stated there." The trust centre renders only behind a script and could not be read.
independent_audit.scope: Requesty security page, for the Requesty API
